humanities_role_explanation: Culturally specific community questions (history, religion, customs, food, etc.) supply the items, but the competence measured is generic multilingual long-form answer quality (correct language, no repetition, factuality via VeriScore, relevance). It does not test disciplinary humanities competence such as historical or literary interpretation.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only: questions in 23 languages with long-form text answers generated by LLMs; optional English translations and reference answers.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Long-form question answering (LFQA) on culturally specific questions; model answers are judged for surface-level quality (wrong language, repetition), factual precision (claim extraction and verification via VeriScore), and relevance (LLM-as-a-judge), plus human ratings/rankings by native speakers. Cultural knowledge is needed, but evaluation focuses on factuality and form.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to a single task (long-form QA) on culturally specific questions.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Claude-3-Opus, Gemini-1.5-Pro, GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-4o, Aya-Expanse-32B, Llama-3-70B, Mixtral-8x22B.

quantitative_metrics.note: Wrong-language rate, repetition rate, factual precision, relevance, combined overall score S, human ratings (1-5) and rankings.

summary: CaLMQA is a translation-free dataset of 51.7K culturally specific long-form questions across 23 languages, collected from community forums and written by hired native speakers for low-resource languages. Seven LLMs are evaluated with automatic surface/factuality/relevance metrics and with native-speaker human evaluation on five languages. Culturally specific questions yield less factual answers than culturally agnostic ones, and low-resource languages suffer severe surface-level errors.
key_findings: Factual precision is 64-71% for culturally agnostic vs 45-52% for culturally specific answers. Open-weight models perform far worse on low-resource languages (mostly below 10 vs 22-66 for closed models). GPT-4o and GPT-4-Turbo have the highest overall score (56.9 on agnostic). Humans prefer GPT-4-Turbo, and omissions and factuality issues strongly predict ratings.
facets_explanation: Questions were collected by Prolific crowdworkers from community forums or written by Upwork native speakers (no disciplinary training), then filtered by GPT-4o-mini and reviewed by authors. Reference answers are optional (real forum answers for 923 questions; Kirundi answers written by hired speakers). Evaluation uses VeriScore against Google Search evidence, LLM-judge relevance, and human ratings rather than matching a single key. Cultural specificity is defined relative to a culture or region, so correctness varies by community.
results_explanation: Table 2 (agnostic / specific): GPT-4O overall score S "56.9 / 49.2" and GPT-4-TURBO "56.9 / 48.7". The paper states that factual precision for agnostic answers is 64%–71% vs 45%–52% for specific; the largest per-model gap is GEMINI-1.5-PRO factual precision 71.1 vs 48.7, about 22 points, but the largest gap reported in the overall score S is GPT-4O 56.9 vs 49.2. The 19-point gap is GPT-4O factual precision 69.6 vs 52.2 rounded from 17.4; correct this to roughly 17-22 depending on model. Headline score 56.9 is the combined S metric (not accuracy). No human baseline is quantified.

humanities_role.quote: We define culturally specific questions as those that refer to concepts unique to one or a few cultures, or have different answers depending on the cultural or regional context.

dataset_size.quote: a dataset of 51.7K culturally specific questions across 23 different languages

evaluation_set_size.quote: we assemble an evaluation set of 3,644 questions from three sources

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: Each model is prompted with a question from our dataset in a zero-shot setup without instructions.

gold_source.quote: we ask English-proficient Prolific3 crowdworkers from different countries to provide a link to a community web forum

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: Then, we apply the claim extraction and verification pipeline introduced in Song et al. (2024)
using Google Search to obtain evidence

gold_community_dependent.quote: have different answers depending on the cultural or regional context

answer_multiplicity.quote: we employ LLM-as-a-Judge (Zheng et al., 2023) using GPT-4O

reported_format_gap_kind.quote: culturally agnostic questions tend to be more factual (64%–71%) than answers to culturally specific questions (45%–52%)

reported_cultural_asymmetry.quote: answers to culturally specific questions contain more factual errors than answers to culturally agnostic questions
